typography.usage: Titles and short section openings; source slide 8 / navTiming.
Reading text, supporting labels and detailed explanations; source slide 8 / navTiming.

recognitionRules: Use Avenir headings on warm paper with a restrained amber timing cue.
Make the planned total duration prominent without implying a measured rehearsal.
Give each scene a clear purpose, visual and spoken cue.
Keep local prototype captures labeled as demonstration material.

principles: Use short action sentences; follow an invitation with a concrete material, choice or check.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: Show the scope. Then show the evidence. Leave time for the question.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid promises that every participant will master the skill.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: Try one version, then compare it with the criterion.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use THREE MINUTE STORY in Avenir with six small scene bars and a separate 03:00 descriptor. The timing is an application label, not part of every logo lockup.
invariants: Use Avenir headings on warm paper with a restrained amber timing cue.
Make the planned total duration prominent without implying a measured rehearsal.
Give each scene a clear purpose, visual and spoken cue.
adaptations: A rehearsal sheet may show all six scenes together.
A presentation version shows one scene at a time and keeps fallback notes separate.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.
